summary: The agent completed P1.M7.T2.S3 fully and correctly (sweep, G1 re-run, sign-off, commits eb4cd58 + c48160a, tree clean) and DID emit {"result":"success"} — but the orchestrator never saw it. A background-job completion notice (job-finished custom message) landed ~4ms after the final assistant message, so pi's print mode (which only prints when the LAST state message is an assistant message) wrote NOTHING to stdout and exited 0. With stdout empty and the tree legitimately clean (the item's job was commit discipline), the orchestrator fell through to no_op.
takeaway: pi -p can exit 0 with EMPTY stdout when a background-job notification is appended just after the final assistant message (print-mode.js only prints if state.messages[last].role === 'assistant'; a trailing custom message suppresses all output). Signature: an attempt log containing only the lone 'Warning: No project session found with id ...' line. Before treating such an item as a no-op, check the agent's session file (prd-sv transcript <sid> --last 5, or run verify_verdict_scan on it) — the verdict JSON is usually sitting there. Longer-term fix worth pinging the human about: print mode should walk back past trailing custom messages to the last assistant message, and/or the orchestrator's verdict scan should retry for ~1s on the session file before declaring no signal.
root_cause: Harness/tooling capture race, evidence: (1) attempt log plan/008_a47116bb2b79/P1M7T2S3/supervisor/attempt-20261124-001428-no_op.log is exactly 100 bytes = the stderr session-creation warning; the agent's ~3KB final message with {"result":"success"} never reached stdout. (2) Session file .../2026-11-24T04-58-47-050Z_prd-impl-P1M7T2S3.jsonl: final assistant message ts 05:14:28.020Z, then a custom_message 'job-finished' (G1 15-suite background re-run) ts 05:14:28.024Z, then background-tasks-state ts 05:14:28.098Z. (3) pi dist/modes/print-mode.js: const lastMessage = state.messages[state.messages.length - 1]; if (lastMessage?.role === 'assistant') writeRawStdout(...) — a trailing custom message (custom_message entries project into state.messages per session-manager.js sessionEntryToContextMessages) makes it print nothing, exit 0. (4) Because the PRP's whole point was commit discipline, git diff/untracked were empty, so the orchestrator's 'changed files but no signal' verify check-in path never fired either. (5) Work verified real: git show --stat eb4cd58 (sweep fixes + plan dirs incl. research/sweep_matrix.md) and c48160a (92-line sign-off); row 7 pointer fixed, G6 line verbatim x1, 14 rows, sign-off self-contained (date + HEAD sha); git diff HEAD on README/ACCEPTANCE/config.toml empty; branch main.
agent_guidance: Your previous attempt SUCCEEDED but the pipeline never saw your success signal: your final message (with {"result":"success"}) was suppressed because a background-job completion notice landed milliseconds after it, so pi printed nothing to stdout; and since your (correct!) commit discipline left the tree clean, the orchestrator had no fallback signal and marked the item no_op. DO NOT redo any work. (2) Then reply with a SHORT summary and end with the exact JSON {"result":"success","message":"P1.M7.T2.S3 complete: work already committed as eb4cd58 + c48160a on main; gates re-confirmed."} as the ABSOLUTE LAST thing in your message — no prose, no fences needed, nothing after it. (3) CRITICAL for this and every future turn in this pipeline: finish ALL background jobs BEFORE your final reply (no run_in_background/monitor task may still be running or notify after your last message) — a late job notification after your final message erases the pipeline's only success signal and fails the item. If anything is genuinely broken, output {"result":"issue","message":"..."} instead.
